version: v1 (checked against upstream dolevf/Damn-Vulnerable-GraphQL-Application release 2.2.0, published 2025-05-24, branch master; Docker Hub dolevf/dvga tags seen: latest and 2.2.0 both updated 2025-05-24, older 2.1.2/2.1.1/2.1.0/2.0.0; use image dolevf/dvga:2.2.0; entries are deliberately coarse: component + class + mechanism, no line numbers)
task_goal_template: Map and hunt the highest-signal security weaknesses of the deliberately vulnerable GraphQL training application at {url}: GraphQL information disclosure, injection (SQL, OS command, stored XSS), server-side request forgery, authorization bypass and arbitrary file write. Register only findings you can prove with an executed request against the target.
notes: DVGA listens on container port 5013 by default (http://localhost:5013); the host port can be remapped with WEB_PORT, and the app binds to 127.0.0.1 by default.

DVGA has Beginner and Expert modes (selected per request via cookie/header); this ground truth assumes the default (beginner) mode. Expert mode changes exploitation difficulty and may block some of these entries.
All denial-of-service scenarios (batch query, deep recursion, aliases, field duplication, resource-intensive queries) are deliberately excluded so the noise governor is not rewarded for DoS.

Stack-trace error disclosure and log injection / HTML injection are listed by upstream but were not confirmed from the resolver source reviewed, so they are omitted; a finding on them is a discovery candidate to verify by hand.
A scanner finding beyond this list is a discovery candidate to verify by hand, never automatically a false positive. Treat a corpus upgrade as a ground-truth version bump, not a silent edit.

findings.title: GraphQL introspection enabled
findings.proof_hint: POSTing an introspection query (__schema { types { name fields { name } } }) to /graphql returns the full schema including importPaste, systemDebug and uploadPaste

findings.title: GraphiQL interactive IDE exposed
findings.proof_hint: GET /graphiql serves the GraphiQL IDE to an unauthenticated browser session

findings.title: GraphQL field suggestions leak schema names
findings.proof_hint: a query with a misspelled field returns an error containing 'Did you mean <real field>', enabling schema recovery even if introspection is blocked

findings.title: SSRF through the importPaste mutation
findings.proof_hint: importPaste with host/port/path/scheme pointing at an attacker-chosen or loopback/internal URL makes the server fetch it and return the response body as paste content

findings.title: OS command injection in importPaste
findings.proof_hint: shell metacharacters in an importPaste argument cause execution of an injected command (e.g. id) whose output appears in the resulting paste

findings.title: OS command injection in systemDebug (and systemDiagnostics) queries
findings.proof_hint: systemDebug(arg:"; id") (or a chained command in systemDiagnostics' cmd) returns the output of an injected command

findings.title: SQL injection in the pastes query filter argument
findings.proof_hint: a tautology or UNION payload in pastes(filter:"...") changes the result set (e.g. returns private pastes or other table data)

findings.title: Stored XSS through createPaste content/title
findings.proof_hint: a paste created with an HTML/script payload in title or content is returned unescaped and executes or renders as markup when the pastes page is viewed

findings.title: JWT token forgery / trusted-token identity bypass
findings.proof_hint: a forged or tampered JWT (e.g. alg=none or admin identity) passed to me(token:...) makes the server treat the session as admin, after which users returns real password values instead of masked ones

findings.title: Arbitrary file write / path traversal in uploadPaste filename
findings.proof_hint: uploadPaste with a filename containing ../ sequences writes the supplied content outside the intended upload directory

findings.title: GraphQL interface protection / query deny-list bypass
findings.proof_hint: a request crafted to evade the server's interface/deny-list checks (e.g. altered operation name, headers or query shape) gets through where the plain query is rejected
